record.field: Document a conclusion, a decision or a record for the whole team as a knowledge page (document.page). Covers when to document (the user asks, or you propose and the user agrees), the page's shape (title, HTML content, category, summary), and the rule that a team page always passes the approval gate — unlike a personal note, which is yours alone.

# Knowledge — document for the team
A conversation can reach a conclusion worth *sharing*: a decision, a procedure, a summary of a record that colleagues will need. Write it as a `document.page` so the whole team can find it.
**This is not a personal note.** A note (`joplin.note`) is yours alone and is written directly. A page is the company's knowledge and always waits for approval. If the user says "lägg det i mina anteckningar" they mean a note — use the Joplin skill instead.
## When to document
Document when EITHER is true:
1. The user asks you to document, write an article, or "skriv ner det här så att alla kan läsa". 2. You propose documenting and the user agrees.
Never document on your own initiative. If you think something belongs in the team's knowledge base, say so and ask first:
"Det här verkar värt att dokumentera för teamet — ska jag skriva en kunskapsartikel?"
Creating a page is a write to shared knowledge and passes the approval gate. Do not try to route around it.
## How to shape the page
- **Title** — required. Short, specific, findable later. Use the subject, not the word "Dokumentation". Good: "Fakturamatchning för EU-kunder". Bad: "Sammanfattning". - **Content** — HTML. Write what was decided and why, not a transcript. Headings, lists and tables are fine. Keep it self-contained: a colleague who was not in the conversation should understand it. - **Category** — optional. The category the page belongs in. If it does not exist it is created for you — do not create it yourself. - **Summary** — optional. One line describing what the page establishes. It becomes the history entry's summary.
## Which tool to use
- `page_create` — free text. You supply the title and the HTML content. - `page_create_from_record` — you name an Odoo model and a record id; the page documents that record. The model must be one you are allowed to read. - `page_create_from_conversation` — you supply a title and a content that documents the current conversation. The content is required: if there is nothing to document, do not call the tool.
## The history is never yours
`document.page.content` is not stored on the page — it lives in `document.page.history`, and the page points at the latest entry. The model creates that entry for you when you write `content`. Never set `history_head` yourself and never try to write a history row directly.
## After documenting
Confirm briefly and name the page, e.g. "Dokumenterad som *Fakturamatchning för EU-kunder* under *Ekonomi*." Do not paste the page back.
